children: Japan’s producer price growth remained elevated in August 2026, reinforcing expectations that the Bank of Japan may continue on its monetary tightening path despite broader market volatility.

Japan’s Corporate Goods Price Index (CGPI) rose 7.6% Y/Y in August, topping market expectations of 7.4%, slowing slightly from an upwardly revised 7.7% in July (the fastest pace since February 2023), input prices remain near 3.5-year highs due to persistent energy and commodity cost pressures.
On a monthly basis, producer prices fell 0.2%, reversing an upwardly revised 0.4% gain in July to mark the first monthly decline in a year.

Separartely, the Business Survey Index for large manufacturers jumped to +7.6% in Q3 2026, recovering sharply from -1.8% in Q2 and far outpacing forecasts of +2.5%. This represents the strongest rate of improvement since Q4 2021, bolstered by government spending and AI-driven demand for production machinery and semiconductors.
Manufacturing sentiment is projected to maintain its expansionary trend, though moderating to +5.8% in Q4 2026 and +4.9% in Q1 2027.
For FY2027, the BOJ raised its inflation projection to 2.4% (from 2.3%) and upgraded its GDP growth outlook to 0.8% (from 0.7%).
